items.summary: Business: The prospectus dropped Monday morning, keeping a Thanksgiving-week listing in play. OpenAI's next round is reportedly near $1.25 trillion, down from $1.4 trillion talk and nowhere near the $2 trillion some Anthropic investors wanted. items.title: Terra's surprise strength is computer use
items.summary: Models: On Agent's Last Exam, Terra scored slightly above every other OpenAI model, Astra included. It ran at about half Sol's cost, a tenth of Astra's, and three times faster than both. It came close to Opus 5.5's score at one-ninth the price. On most other benchmarks, including agentic coding, it lands slightly below Sol. The early consensus: probably not for writing code, probably yes for computer use.

items.title: OpenAI resumes frontier training inside a quarantined "offline world"
items.summary: Models: All of OpenAI's frontier RL runs will now use an indexed, cached copy of the web so models can't affect external systems, mirroring Anthropic's earlier resumption of frontier training. If it works, training continues. But it also signals that neither lab trusts alignment methods alone to constrain its models and both are reaching for the blunter tool of cutting off the internet.

items.title: Neo labs hedge with locked-in GPUs, as Chamath calls 2027 a clear-out year
items.summary: Compute: Yuchen Jin reports neo labs treating early GPU contracts as a fallback: rental prices are up 2-3×, so failed model bets can resell compute. Chamath, though, calls neoclouds "disorganized and poorly capitalized" and expects stranded compute plus shortages for OpenAI and Anthropic as hyperscaler projects stall. He predicts 2027 will clear out bad bets and consolidate the field.

items.title: A real first profit and a mostly paper $80B loss
items.summary: Business: Q2 brought a $974M GAAP operating profit, Anthropic's first profitable quarter. Gross margin hit 85% in H1, up from 40%, though rising research, sales and admin costs left H1 operating margin at -4.3%. Of the $80B H1 net loss, $72B is a convertible-debt accounting change caused by stock appreciation, not cash going out the door.
